name: XRP Ledger
executive_summary: The XRP Ledger has been running since 2012, designed from the start for fast, low-cost cross-border payments rather than general-purpose computing, and fourteen years later at the time of this scoring that focus shows up in a Real-World Utility score of 86 and a TradFi score of 70. Real-world payment usage and TradFi rail access carry the score, while a small, curated set of roughly 35 validators and token supply that was mostly pre-mined at launch hold it back. The AI score of 65 reflects a ledger with rich built-in payment features but no ability to deploy custom code on top of it, a limitation that's been in place since launch.

key_findings: Carried by real-world payment utility (86) and TradFi rails (81), dragged by premine tokenomics (64) and a permissioned validator set (42).
A detailed four-phase post-quantum roadmap targeting 2028 is documented.
Decentralization (42) -- XRPL's ~35-validator Unique Node List is a curated, permissioned set and a persistent structural weakness.

Privacy & Confidentiality (32) -- the ledger is fully transparent today. XLS-0096 ConfidentialTransfer entered validator voting after the August 6, 2026 rippled v3.3.0 release, and covers Multi-Purpose Tokens only, explicitly not XRP itself.

binding_cap.short_note: Capped by Programmability Tier Partial -- rich native primitives but zero deployable custom logic on mainnet.

key_findings: Sets the calibration precedent for the Programmability Tier Partial/65 floor -- rich native primitives (DEX, AMM, escrow) without deployable custom logic.
Demonstrated the Operational Reliability cool-down timer's positive direction all the way to PASS (12 clean months).
Economic Predictability (85) is XRP's strongest AI category -- fixed near-zero fees, no gas auctions.

watch_items: XLS-0096 ConfidentialTransfer requires greater than 80% validator support sustained for 14 days. Activation would move Privacy & Confidentiality, though the native-asset limitation would still apply.
XLS-0101 convention -- parallel watch item that could lift the Deterministic Finality or Programmability Tier cap.
CLARITY Act pending Senate floor action -- would convert agency-level guidance into statutory regulatory clarity.
